metrics.headline: QK-norm + undetached dyn q-temp vs both parents across head splits: NOT strictly better; hd4 rescue 0.9387

config.title: Is QK-norm + undetached dynamic query temperature a strictly better parametrisation? The full head-split sweep
config.hypothesis: 2026-08-06 closed the hd=4 QK-norm cliff (98% rescue) with an UNDETACHED per-token query temperature tau = clamp(r_t/EMA)^alpha, but only at the cliff config. "Strictly better parametrisation" needs the whole curve: 2026-07-30 showed QK-norm helps at hd=16..64, is a small tax at hd=128, and is a big tax at hd=4 — and detached dynq cost +0.011 at hd=32 (2026-08-02), so undetached do-no-harm is genuinely open. Tonight: rerun the full 2026-07-30 head-split sweep (hd 4/16/32/64/128 at d_model=128, paired inits, shared batch stream, 2 seeds) with three arms — baseline (no norm), plain qknorm, and the composite (qknorm + undetached dynq). Predictions if "strictly better" is true: composite matches or beats BOTH parents at every split, keeps the hd=4 closure, keeps qknorm's mid-range win, and the U-curve's interior optimum stays (or moves left); if the composite instead pays a mid-range tax, the 08-06 rescue is cliff-specific machinery, not a better parametrisation.
